description: Give the agent eyes: pull frames or a contact sheet out of a video as PNG so the result can be inspected (caption placement, logo position, crop, colour).

argv.description: raw CLI arguments (non-canonical compatibility path; when present every other key is ignored)

at.description: time of a frame to extract (repeatable)

compare.description: second video: place its frame next to the first (needs --at)

compare_at.description: seek time in the comparison file, one per --at. By default both use --at.

dry_run.description: print the ffmpeg commands that would run, run nothing

fast.description: preview quality: x264 preset veryfast (overrides --preset) for quick iterations

guides.description: draw broadcast safe-area outlines on the PNG (a preview only; nothing is written into a video): a comma list of action (93%%), title (90%%) and 4:3 (the 4:3 centre cut of a 16:9 frame, with its 90%% action and 80%% title safe)

ink.description: measure non-background pixels in each written PNG (bbox, ink_fraction, row_bands per tile for a contact sheet) instead of just eyeballing it -- a pixel-only signal, not a legibility judgement

json_brief.description: like --json but trimmed: status, output, dry_run, verified, a compact summary of the output probe, this tool's own keys, and the command count instead of the command lines (failures print the full failure document, unchanged)

no_timecode.description: no burnt-in timecode stamps (a way out if drawtext itself is unusable, see doctor)

output.description: output PNG (contact sheet / compare) or basename for --at frames

overwrite.description: allow replacing an existing output (refused without it)

plan.description: write the dry run as a plan (inputs fingerprinted, commands, expected output, verify steps) that render.py FILE executes later; implies --dry-run

safe.description: shade the zones this platform's UI covers (its description bar, like column, status bar) so you can see whether anything readable is under them

tiles.description: contact sheet grid COLSxROWS, e.g. 4x3 for 12 frames (default 4x3)

timeout.description: kill an ffmpeg run past this many seconds, kind=timeout (default 1800; 0 = no limit)

width.description: total width of the sheet / compare image in px, 2..16384 (default 1280); an --at frame is at most this wide and never enlarged

name: look
